b: Don’t assume a nodding head is a commitment.
Lack of commitment shows up as resistance. People who aren’t committed talk about tomorrow, problems, and others.
Help people find their own reasons to commit.
What isn’t working as well as you’d like?
What’s frustrating about the current situation?
What concerns you most about continuing this way?
Don’t declare the problem first. People are motivated to solve problems they see.
What would you like to be different?
Who would benefit if you succeeded?
Why is that important to you?
What makes this goal worth the effort?
How does this connect with the person you want to become?
What makes you believe you could succeed?
When have you succeeded with challenges in the past?
What strengths can you rely on?
What support would increase your confidence?
What would you have to give up?
What are you willing to do?
On a scale of 1-10, how committed are you to do this?
Reveal existing motivation. When their number is 6 or less, ask, “Why a 6 instead of a 3?” Explore ways to strengthen commitment.
Vague promises provide cover for the uncommitted.
Don’t ask for a yes before people discover their why.
Which question could strengthen commitment on your team today?
